**Proposed mechanism:** COL1A2 (HGNC:2200) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular Matrix Organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular Matrix Organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac Valvular Abnormalities (HP:0001657); HMOX1 (HGNC:4776) —DISRUPTS→ Heme (CHEBI:17907); Heme (CHEBI:17907) —DECREASES→ Biliverdin (CHEBI:17303); HMOX1 (HGNC:4776) —INCREASES→ Oxidative Stress (HP:0011440); Biliverdin (CHEBI:17303) —BINDS→ Extracellular Matrix Organization (GO:0030198); Oxidative Stress (HP:0011440) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular Matrix Organization (GO:0030198). Loss-of-function mutations in COL1A2 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to cardiac valvular abnormalities (Disease A). Loss-of-function mutations in HMOX1 impair heme catabolism, leading to decreased biliverdin production and increased heme accumulation (oxidative stress). This oxidative stress, in turn, disrupts extracellular matrix organization, converging with the primary defect in Disease A and potentially exacerbating valvular issues.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal no significant enrichment of HMOX1 variants in patients with cardiac valvular abnormalities beyond what is expected by chance, or if interventions targeting oxidative stress do not ameliorate cardiac valvular phenotypes in HMOX1 deficiency models, this hypothesis would be weakened.

**Why it matters:** Targeting oxidative stress pathways downstream of HMOX1 could offer a therapeutic strategy for Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, cardiac valvular type, by mitigating secondary damage to the extracellular matrix.

#### 2. autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome type 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.393)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6785807)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL1A2 (HGNC:2205) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac valvular abnormalities (HP:0001648); FAS (HGNC:3004) —DISRUPTS→ Apoptosis signaling pathway (GO:0006915); FASLG (HGNC:3005) —DISRUPTS→ Apoptosis signaling pathway (GO:0006915); Apoptosis signaling pathway (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ Lymphadenopathy (HP:0002710); Apoptosis signaling pathway (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ Autoimmune phenomena (HP:0000623). Loss-of-function mutations in COL1A2 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to cardiac valvular abnormalities characteristic of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, cardiac valvular type. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in FAS (or its ligand FASLG) disrupt the apoptosis signaling pathway, resulting in lymphadenopathy and autoimmune phenomena seen in autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome type 1. The shared convergence is the dysregulation of the apoptosis signaling pathway, which, while primarily causative in ALPS1, can also indirectly influence connective tissue integrity and immune responses relevant to EDS.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in COL1A2 in patients diagnosed with autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome type 1, or pathogenic variants in FAS/FASLG in patients diagnosed with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, cardiac valvular type, without any other identifiable genetic cause for their respective conditions. _(variant: A common (AF > 0.01) pathogenic variant in COL1A2, FAS, or FASLG in the general population would challenge its role as a causal gene for these rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the Fas/FasL pathway in both conditions could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting apoptosis or immune dysregulation that might benefit patients with either Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, cardiac valvular type, or autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome type 1.

**Proposed mechanism:** COL1A2 (HGNC:2204) —DISRUPTS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac valvular abnormalities (HP:0001659); IL2RG (HGNC:5537) —DISRUPTS→ T cell activation (GO:0042110); T cell activation (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002703). **Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct cellular modules disrupted in these diseases highlights the importance of maintaining extracellular matrix integrity for cardiovascular health and proper immune cell function for immune competence. Therapeutic strategies could involve targeting downstream pathways affected by ECM dysfunction or immune cell signaling defects, potentially revealing novel treatment avenues for related conditions.
